_activity: From a 4 to a 5: pairing documents
_licence: ORIGINAL, built on the 11.2 casefile documents (numbered per the signed 11.2 map). Quotes are the casefile's adapted text.
design_intent: Not skill practice. A kid here already writes at a 4. This is the gold dust that turns a 4 into a 5: more content, a wider lens, and a named technique.

tidbits.text: Washington's 1786 warning about anarchy was a private letter to Madison. People tend to say what they really think in private, which is part of what makes a letter like that strong evidence.

Captain Preston wrote his account of the Boston Massacre in jail, while he faced a murder charge. A detail from an account like that proves what he claimed, not always what happened. A 5 says which one.
Documents 4 and 5 describe the same night in Boston two different ways. That's the Similarity/Difference relationship the 11.2 short essay uses.

exemplars.text: In Document 11, the Articles say taxes “shall be laid and collected by the legislatures of the several states,” which shows Congress was weak.

In Document 11, the Articles say taxes “shall be laid and collected by the legislatures of the several states,” so Congress had to wait for the states to pay; Washington's private warning in Document 12 that “we are fast heading toward anarchy and confusion” shows what that weakness looked like by 1786.
exemplars.what_changed: The 4 uses one document well. The 5 pairs it with a second document that shows the result, so the evidence builds instead of just sitting there.

techniques.name: Pair two documents
techniques.explanation: Use one document for the cause and one for the effect, or two that disagree. Two documents talking to each other are stronger than one alone.

techniques.name: Source the detail
techniques.explanation: Say who wrote it and why before you use it. “In a private letter” or “at his own trial” changes what the detail proves.

try_it.prompt: Find a review, an ad or a post today. What's the one exact detail you'd quote to prove what it's really trying to get you to do?
try_it.status: Untimed, optional, never scored, never saved — practice reflection only.
